verdict.rationale: Make documents its own webhook queue: instead of running immediately, a scenario can be scheduled to process accumulated webhook requests periodically. That is a native way to defer and batch executions, but the evidence never frames it as rate-limit throttling and shows no execution-rate or concurrency controls. Missing for 10: configurable throttling/rate caps per scenario or per downstream app, concurrency limits, explicit rate-limit handling (e.g. backoff on 429), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can throttle or queue workflow executions to respect downstream rate limits

citations.quote: If you don't want to run your immediately after a webhook receives data, you can schedule your to process all webhook requests periodically
the whole queue is then processed every time your schedule criteria are met
